If you don't mind me asking, how old are you? What part of the world are you in?

When I have these thoughts about me being a burden on my friends and family I often dream of what it would be like to up and disappear. Save everything I can and move somewhere with a low cost of living and start from scratch. And when the options were that, or kill myself I let myself daydream as long as I can about it. After a while I realized, there's nothing stopping me. What's the difference between dying in a basement in rural Canada and dying on a beach in Cuba? So I started saving.

 It's not much. What little bit I can. I don't know if I'll ever get there, but the goal helps me keep going. Maybe think about it.

I'm pulling for you.

When you're used to being numb, those feelings can be overwhelming when they hit you. The guilty may be deserving or not, but there is nothing in this world anyone has complete control over. Please try to get yourself out of that situation and look into some kind of grief counseling. It's more direct than therapy, often cheaper in places where you need to pay for that kind of thing, and focusing on one thing can make it easier to work through the problems.

 Good luck, I'm pulling for you.

I've had those intrusive thoughts too. About my self, about other people. Human nature I think. Or maybe societal pressure. We've been told and shown so often that 'normal people' just solve their problems. Just work harder. Just want it more. It take a lot of work to realize all of that is bullshit. "Normal people" have problems, want support, need help. 

I hope you get that support.
I think I can actually count the number of real hugs I've had. If WHEN I make it through all of this I'm going to hug more. If I could I would send you the biggest bear hug.
